claim.quote: NaI-33 has a record low $^{39}$K contamination of 4.3$\pm$0.2 ppb as determined by mass spectrometry. We measured a light yield of 11.1$\pm$0.2 photoelectrons/keV and an energy resolution of 13.2% (FWHM/E) at 59.5 keV.

key_value_text.quote: A cut-based strategy and a multivariate approach indicated a rate, attributed to the intrinsic radioactivity of the crystal, of $\sim$1 count/day/kg/keV in the [5-20] keV region.
key_value_text.value: A cut-based strategy and a multivariate approach indicated a rate, attributed to the intrinsic radioactivity of the crystal, of $\sim$1 count/day/kg/keV in the [5-20] keV region.

name: Characterization of SABRE crystal NaI-33 with direct underground counting

summary.plain: The first characterisation of a 3.4 kg SABRE crystal, NaI-33, in a passive shield at Gran Sasso: a record low potassium contamination, a good light yield and a low rate from its own radioactivity.
summary.technical: Underground counting of NaI-33 at LNGS (Hall B facility): 39K 4.3 +- 0.2 ppb (mass spectrometry), light yield 11.1 +- 0.2 photoelectrons/keV, 226Ra 5.9 +- 0.6 and 228Th 1.6 +- 0.3 uBq/kg, 210Pb out of equilibrium 0.51 +- 0.02 mBq/kg, alpha quenching factor 0.63 +- 0.01 at 5304 keV; about 1 count/day/kg/keV in the [5-20] keV region (Eur. Phys. J. C 81, 299).

title: Characterization of SABRE crystal NaI-33 with direct underground counting
why_it_matters: It is the first published characterisation of the crystal that the SABRE team later ran in the Proof-of-Principle detector.
